attributes.refutation_detail: The refuted record's RANKING is sound and its per-function blockers reproduce verbatim at HEAD; what is refuted is the inference from its ranking key to the phrase 'one function from a flip'. CX states its key explicitly - 'primary = OPEN FUNCTIONS REMAINING (total_functions - matched_functions) ascending, because a flip needs every function closed and the distance to one is a COUNT of functions' - and that last clause is the error. A flip also needs every DATA section claimed, and the function count cannot see an unclaimed one. CX itself anticipates the general shape of this: it was written to refute a CODE-PERCENT band for being blind to a distance measured in functions, and it then adopted a FUNCTION count that is blind to a distance measured in sections. AGENTS.md residual-work discipline 10 already requires that 'any closing X flips the file claim must carry a live datadiff --sections result, not an assumption'; CX's roster carried none, and the three lanes it dispatched inherited the assumption.

falsifier: Re-run `python tools/gdl/datadiff.py --sections <unit>` on each candidate. A run in which game/sound/sounds_evt and game/world/newcam report '0 blocker(s)' refutes this claim - either because the data claims landed or because the tool's size comparison was wrong. Independently: if a TU with a nonzero `<- FLIP BLOCKER` line is ever successfully promoted to Object(Matching) with a green `build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK`, then these rows are not flip blockers and the claim is void.

MEASURED AT COMMIT a4aa124f0 with `python tools/gdl/datadiff.py --sections <unit>`, one call per unit, over the three TUs work_claim.flipdist-closes.20260904.v1 dispatched as 'each ONE function from a flip'. ONLY ONE OF THE THREE IS.

game/audio/dcsdrv - '1 object data section(s) compared, 0 blocker(s)'; `.data: size 0xB8, 100.0% bytes equal`, extab 24 bytes 100.0000% matched, extabindex 36 bytes 100.0000% matched. This TU IS one function from a flip: close dcsHandleRequest and nothing else is owed.

game/sound/sounds_evt - '2 object data section(s) compared, 2 blocker(s)': `.data: SIZE target 0x0 vs ours 0x104 <- FLIP BLOCKER - OURS is LARGER than the target` and `.sdata2: SIZE target 0x0 vs ours 0x8C <- FLIP BLOCKER`. extab 920 bytes 89.8913% matched, extabindex 1380 bytes n/a. So AudioSetupBossStreams' one-instruction ADDR16_LO home copy is NOT the only thing between this TU and a flip; it also owes two unclaimed data sections totalling 0x190 bytes that our object emits and the split map does not assign to it.

game/world/newcam - '2 object data section(s) compared, 2 blocker(s)': `.rodata: SIZE target 0x0 vs ours 0x26 <- FLIP BLOCKER` and `.sdata2: SIZE target 0x0 vs ours 0xC8 <- FLIP BLOCKER`. extab 152 bytes 53.9474% matched, extabindex 228 bytes n/a. Same verdict: fn_8006DC64 is necessary but not sufficient.

CORROBORATION FROM A SECOND INSTRUMENT, taken independently before datadiff was run. `defake_gate.py baseline <unit> --at-head` prints a DATA baseline per TU, and its counts agree: dcsdrv '3 non-text section(s), 244/244 matched bytes'; sounds_evt '4 non-text section(s), 0/2300 matched bytes ... .data 0/0; .sdata2 0/0; extab 0/920; extabindex 0/1380'; newcam '4 non-text section(s), 0/380 matched bytes ... .rodata 0/0; .sdata2 0/0; extab 0/152; extabindex 0/228'. Two tools, one verdict. Note the two disagree in PRESENTATION in a way that matters: defake_gate renders an unclaimed section as `0/0`, which reads as 'nothing there, nothing owed', while datadiff renders the same state as `SIZE target 0x0 vs ours 0x104 <- FLIP BLOCKER`. A lane reading only the gate line would conclude the opposite of the truth.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME CLASS OF ERROR CX WAS WRITTEN TO FIX. The precedent is game/audio/dcsdrv itself: attempt.DC_dcshandlerequest-jumptable-settled-and-webfrank-barred.20260901.v1 closed that TU's data half by adding ONE `.data` line to config/GUNE5D/splits.txt (commit 767ec66bf) and only then could its data read 100%. The two TUs above are at the state dcsdrv was in BEFORE that commit, and the work is the same shape: identify the target range each emitted section corresponds to and claim it in splits.txt, then re-run datadiff --sections.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DISPATCH, stated so the next order does not repeat it. A flip-distance roster must rank on TWO numbers, not one: open FUNCTIONS and open DATA SECTIONS, and it must print the `datadiff --sections` blocker count beside each row. The remaining three distance-1 units CX names (game/mb/mb_camera, game/pb/dbgtext, game/pb/pb_frame) were NOT measured by this lane and must not be assumed clean - the base rate observed here is two in three.
